summary: The focused PIT examples now capture Maven output, but their archival flow can preserve a prior mutation report as evidence for a failed current run.

findings.title: Focused PIT examples can archive a stale mutation report
findings.trigger: In a normal shell without errexit, a previous PIT run has left `core/target/pit-reports/mutations.xml`, and the documented Maven invocation then fails during `test-compile` or PIT startup before producing a new report.
findings.consequence: The unconditional copy places the old XML beside the new failure log. A later delivery-ledger record can therefore attribute old mutation results to the current failed or inconclusive change.
findings.evidence: `verification/pit.md:71-72` copies any existing target XML without first invalidating it; the same sequence appears at `verification/pit.md:100-101`. In contrast, `scripts/run-pit-core.sh:194-220` deletes the prior report before running and archives only afterward, and `scripts/tests/test_run_pit_core.py:70-81` covers this exact stale-report failure. `verification/delivery-ledger.md:46-50` consumes the archived XML as PIT evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Before each inline invocation, remove or otherwise invalidate the target report and use a fresh or artifact-empty evidence directory. Copy XML only after confirming that the current run produced it, and surface a missing XML as inconclusive rather than silently retaining prior evidence.
